title: Demonstratives and Waw
description: Demonstratives identify a referent as “this” or “that.” The conjunction waw attaches to a word and links phrases or clauses.

blocks.html: Demonstrative forms agree with nouns in gender and number, and they can appear alone or next to a noun. Waw commonly means “and,” but it can also introduce contrast, consequence, or a main clause after a dependent clause. Its vowels change in some environments. Identify waw as a prefix, then choose its English function from the relationship between the linked clauses.

didYouKnow: According to OSHB/MorphHB (CC BY 4.0), the most frequent word in this unit is וְ (wə), occurring 12080 times in the Westminster Leningrad Codex.
